Which system of record issues the authoritative identifier for this decision occurrence, and what is that identifier?
If no master-system reference exists, which governed IRI or Dimension-minted UUID/ULID identifies it, and who mints it?
How is this identifier kept distinct from the identifiers of the subject, the decision notice and the applied rule set?
Under which later events (correction, re-vote, appeal outcome) does the identifier stay stable rather than being reissued?
What exact question does this decision answer, and whose formulation of it is authoritative?
Which subject entities, requests or assets does the decision reach, and by which references?
Which answers were admissible before the choice was made?
Is one occurrence a single approval step, a whole approval chain, or one item within a multi-item session?
Which decision-type code, from which governed code list and version, classifies this occurrence?
Was the outcome produced solely by automated processing, by a human, or by a human acting on an automated recommendation?
Which materiality or impact tier applies, and which scale sets that tier?
Is the decision reversible in practice, and what makes it irreversible once acted upon?
Which instrument confers the power to take this decision, and what is its citation, version and effective date?
Which position or role, rather than which individual, holds the decision right under that instrument?
Which agent acted on behalf of which responsible agent, under what delegation instrument and validity period?
Which act is reserved to the holder and cannot be delegated to a designated representative?
Which value, risk-class, subject-matter or jurisdictional limits bound the authority applied?
What is the escalation path when a request exceeds the holder's limit?
Under what emergency conditions may a limit be exceeded, and what after-the-fact ratification is required?
How is the limit check evidenced at decision time rather than asserted afterwards?
Which agents participated, in which roles, and with what share of responsibility for the outcome?
How is the design-time decision owner or decision maker in the rule model distinguished from the agent who actually decided this occurrence?
Who is accountable for the decision after it is taken, if that differs from who signed it?
Which participants' acts were required for completion and which were advisory only?
Which separation-of-duties rule applies, and which role pairs are incompatible for this decision type?
Is dual authorization or two-person control required, and on which criterion is that requirement triggered?
How are declared conflicts of interest, recusals and abstentions recorded, and what effect do they have on validity?
How is a self-approval or maker-equals-checker violation detected and recorded?
What quorum and majority threshold made this decision validly constituted?
Which voting method was used, and how were abstentions, proxies and absentees counted?
What were the counted results for, against and abstaining?
How were decisions taken by written procedure or by chair's action subsequently ratified?
Which inputs, documents and datasets were actually used, at which version or as-of time?
Where did each input come from and who attested to its accuracy?
What was missing, stale or uncertain at decision time, and how was that gap treated?
How is the package fixed so that later changes at the source do not silently alter what was decided upon?
Which rule set, policy or decision model was applied, at which pinned version?
Who owns that rule set, and is this decision permitted to depart from it?
If the decision departed from the criteria, what deviation reason and additional approval were recorded?
Where more than one rule matched, which resolution or hit policy determined the result?
Which options were on the table when the choice was made?
Which option was chosen and what stated reason rejected each of the others?
Was the null option of deferring or taking no action admissible, and was it considered?
How is an option added late in the process distinguished from one available from the outset?
What reasoning connects the inputs and applied criteria to the chosen option?
Which explanation is owed to the affected party, in what form and within what period?
How complete must the rationale be for the decision to be effectively contestable?
Where automated components contributed, what is recorded about their role, logic and limits?
Which deliberation events took place, when, and who attended each?
Which dissenting or minority positions were recorded, and by whom?
Which parts of the deliberation are confidential and which are disclosable?
Who certified the minutes and when were they approved?
What is the outcome value, from which governed outcome vocabulary and version?
How does the outcome map to the referenced authorization model's decision values, and where does that mapping lose meaning?
How are 'no applicable authority' and 'could not decide' distinguished from an explicit refusal?
At what instant did the decision take effect, and how does that differ from when it was recorded?
Which conditions, limitations and restrictions attach to the outcome, and which of them are binding rather than advisory?
Which obligations must the recipient discharge, by when, and what follows if they are not discharged?
From when until when is the decision valid, and is validity time-driven, event-driven or open-ended?
Which events trigger mandatory review or automatic lapse of the decision?
To whom must the outcome be communicated, in what form, and within what period?
How are receipt of the notice and acceptance of its terms evidenced, and what happens if acknowledgement fails?
Which downstream system consumes this decision, and what exactly is in the hand-over payload?
Which model owns enforcement of the outcome, and how is drift between the decided outcome and the enforced state detected?
What are the permitted states of the decision occurrence and which transitions between them are legal?
Which state means decided but not yet effective, and which means effective but suspended?
Who may cause each transition, and may that differ from who took the original decision?
How is each transition timestamped, and by whose clock and offset?
Which decision supersedes or revokes which, and from what effective instant?
What happens to obligations and rights created by the superseded or revoked decision?
Which elapsed periods or events force reauthorization rather than amendment?
Is retroactive revocation permitted here, and what evidence must support it?
Who is assigned oversight of this automated or assisted decision, and with what competence and means to intervene?
Was the automated output disregarded, overridden or reversed, and on what basis?
On what legal or policy basis is a solely automated decision permitted for this decision type?
What evidence shows the human intervention was substantive rather than a formality?
Who may contest this decision, on what grounds, and within what period?
How does the review outcome relate to the original decision: confirm, amend, replace or remit?
Which body reviews the decision, and must it be independent of the original decider?
How are emergency overrides and after-the-fact ratifications of this decision recorded?
Which agent was associated with the decision activity, in which role, and following which plan or procedure version?
What are the start and end times of the decision activity, and how are they distinguished from recording or ingestion time?
Which prior activities informed this decision and which entities did it generate?
How is a provenance assertion made by the deciding system distinguished from one asserted by a third party?
What meaning is attached to each signature: review, approval, responsibility or authorship?
Which signer identity is bound to the signature, and how was that identity authenticated?
How is the signature bound to the record so it cannot be excised, copied or transferred to another record?
Which model verifies the signature, and where is the verification result referenced from here?
Which retention class and schedule apply to the decision record and, separately, to its deliberation content?
Which model or policy executes disposition, and what does this model keep as a tombstone afterwards?
What blocks destruction while the decision still confers rights or imposes obligations?
How are erasure requests for personal data reconciled with the obligation to keep the decision record?
Which parties may read the outcome, the rationale and the deliberation, and on what basis each?
Which personal data appear in the decision context, and under what lawful basis are they held?
What confidentiality marking applies to each part, and who may downgrade it?
Which mandatory disclosures to a data subject, auditor, supervisory authority or court override the default restriction?
Which external vocabularies is this decision context mapped to, and at which versions?
Where does the mapping to authorization decision values lose or distort meaning?
What evidence would be required before claiming conformance to any of these standards?
Who maintains each mapping and when was it last checked against the source version?

requirements: Run a separate no-tools adversarial audit of the active provider result.
Verify the model boundary and entry kind against the frozen relationship contract.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Expose the owner-authorized provider waiver in every publication artifact.
Keep the result reviewable-draft while independent second-provider review is waived.
